title: Scaling of Fourier coefficients
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability law $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose $\Omega$ has a real orthonormal basis indexed by $\iota$ under $\pi$, with one basis vector equal to the constant function $1$. For every real scalar $c$, function $f:(\Omega^n)\to\mathbb R$, and multi-index $a\in\iota^n$, the Fourier coefficient of $cf$ at $a$ is $c$ times the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $a$.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$\iota$ is finite, nonempty, and has decidable equality
The basis is indexed by $\iota$ and spans the real-valued functions on $\Omega$
The basis vector at the distinguished index is constant $1$
